text:
liz: heads-up — saw a short but sharp perf regression in the continuous-formation path around 10:05–10:15UTC. batch_utilization dropped ~30%, queue depth spiked, and tokens/sec fell. attaching quick profiler notes :eyes:

omar: saw the alert too. can you paste the exact queries/metrics you used? want to reproduce in grafana.

liz: quick PromQL-ish checks i ran (pseudo):

```
# formation throughput
sum(rate(continuous_formation_tokens_total[1m])) by (model, pool)
# batch util (0..1)
avg_over_time(continuous_formation_batch_utilization[5m])
# queue depth percentiles
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(continuous_formation_queue_depth_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
# kernel switches
sum(rate(kernel_switches_total[5m])) by (model)
# kv cache hitrate by prefix length
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (prefix_len) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m])) by (prefix_len)
```

nina: dashboard sketch ideas:
- panel: batch formation latency heatmap (x=wait_ms, y=seq_len_bucket)
- panel: queue depth p50/p90/p99 (per pool & route)
- panel: tokens/sec (1m,5m) split by model + kernel variant
- panel: kv_cache_hitrate over time, broken down by prefix_len and route
- panel: kernel_switch_rate + fallback_count (show spikes when we fall back to slower kernels)
alerts: batch_util < 45% for 3m (warning), < 30% for 5m (page). queue_depth p95 > 200 for 5m -> page. kv_hitrate drop > 5ppt relative to baseline -> page.

ryan: +1 on the panels. one caveat: collecting high-cardinality kv_cache by prefix_len will blow up cardinality. suggest sampled timeseries + tag "prefix_len_bucket" (e.g., 1-4,5-16,17-64,65+). also: don't sample counters; sample trace spans for heavy tails.

sahil: re token budgets — we should add two derived metrics: "effective_tokens_per_gpu" and "batch_headroom" (batch_capacity_tokens - observed_tokens). propose token_budget targets: small seq (<=128): target utilization 0.9; mid (129-1024): 0.75; long (>1024): 0.6. if avg_util deviates below target by >0.15 for 10m, autoscale token_budget up by 20% for the next 15m and re-evaluate.

omar: sampling/overhead question: what sampling rate for traces? ryan suggested 1% continuous + 10% burst on anomaly. that seems reasonable. we also need to tag traces with: model, seq_len_bucket, route_id, kernel_variant, kv_hitrate_bucket.

ops-bot: telemetry-probe v2 deployed to staging at 2765440005 by ci/cd :robot_face:

liz: implementation notes:
- nina: can you prototype the grafana panels with the queries above and include heatmap + percentile transforms?
- omar: add a lightweight sampler that emits 1% of formation traces and a separate anomaly hook to temporarily raise to 10%. tag traces as discussed.
- ryan: please add the profiler config for capturing kernel_switch stacks at 10s intervals (only on sampled traces). watch overhead < 1%.
- sahil: compute "effective_tokens_per_gpu" for last 7d and suggest baseline thresholds; add batch_headroom metric and a derived alert rule.

liz: i'll create a follow-up infra PR to add the panels + alert rules and a short runbook for when batch_util falls. will post dashboard UIDs here. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

omar: quick question — do we want to surface a single "formation_health" composite metric (weighted score of batch_util, kv_hitrate, tokens/sec) for a single-glance SLO? that would make oncall life easier.

nina: i like it. keep weights configurable per pool/route. default: 0.5*batch_util + 0.3*kv_hitrate + 0.2*tokens/sec_norm.

liz: agree. include that in the dashboard as the top-level sparkline and add a 3-step runbook for degradation. I'll open the issue and assign owners.

ryan: copying notes into profiling ticket. will try to repro locally with a synthetic mix and kernel-switch heavy workload.

sahil: i'll run historical analysis to find past periods where formation_health < 0.5 and correlate with kernel_switch spikes. will share findings by EOD.

liz: perfect. closing this thread — action items tracked in the issue I'll link. if anyone sees a repeated spike, ping me immediately. :zap:
